records.name: Daniel Boone Park
records.address: 591 Horn in the West Drive, Boone, NC 28607
records.managing_agency: Town of Boone Cultural Resources Department
records.why_major: A 36.5-acre cultural and recreation campus containing major town attractions.
records.coordinate_source: Town of Boone Daniel Boone Park facility-directory map pin

relationship_reconciliation.finding: The current Town facility directory expressly lists Boone Jaycee Park as a subfacility of Daniel Boone Park. Boone Jaycee Park has its own 728 Horn in the West Drive facility record and map pin within the broader campus.
relationship_reconciliation.publication_rule: Retain Daniel Boone Park as the parent. Do not import Boone Jaycee Park as a separate major parent; any future destination treatment must preserve the parent-child relationship and use destination-specific evidence.

current_access_review.finding: The current Town facility page describes ongoing events and public attractions, and the Town held a public park-tour meeting there in May 2026. Boone Jaycee Park separately publishes dawn-to-dusk hours, but no current general hours were found for the entire Daniel Boone Park campus.
current_access_review.publication_rule: Do not extend Boone Jaycee Park's dawn-to-dusk schedule to the full campus or to separately operated attractions. Recheck every named facility before launch-guide publication.

records.name: Junaluska Park
records.why_major: Neighborhood-scale destination selected for its documented town facility status and broad recreation mix.
records.coordinate_precision: address point validated inside the Town GIS 135 Bear Trail commercial structure footprint

address_reconciliation.finding: The current Town facility page lists 135 Bear Trail. The 2023 ADA plan uses 175 Summit Street for inspections performed in 2020, and the facility page's embedded map pin still falls on the Town GIS residential structure at 175 Summit Street. The Town GIS separately maps 135 Bear Trail as a commercial American Legion structure, and the reviewed address point falls inside that footprint.
address_reconciliation.publication_rule: Use 135 Bear Trail as the current visitor address and the reviewed 135 Bear Trail building match as the inventory coordinate. Treat 175 Summit Street and the embedded facility pin as conflicting legacy evidence, not a current public entrance, until the Town corrects or explains the map pin.

current_access_review.finding: The current Town facility page lists parking, restrooms, basketball, soccer, playground, picnic shelters, and a walking track. No current park-specific general hours were found. The 2023 ADA plan records corrective work targets but does not establish that every listed barrier has been remediated.
current_access_review.publication_rule: Do not publish current hours or claim full accessible-route compliance without a new operator check.

records.name: Marvin Caldwell Park
records.why_major: A 24-acre City community park reopened after extensive renovations, with a current splash pad schedule and a documented multi-use recreation role.
records.coordinate_source: City of Concord park-directory address map link

current_access_review.finding: The City explicitly announced on 2026-07-16 that Marvin Caldwell Park reopened after extensive renovations. The notice gives park hours of dawn to dusk and splash-pad hours of Tuesday through Sunday, 10 a.m. to 7 p.m., but does not publish a season end date or a complete current amenity inventory.
current_access_review.publication_rule: Use the reopening notice for access and hours. Recheck the splash-pad schedule and obtain a current as-built amenity list before any launch-guide publication.

source_reconciliation.finding: The park directory still lists the pre-renovation amenity configuration. City Council's final-design record and later construction materials document changes, while the reopening notice confirms extensive renovations without enumerating every completed feature.
source_reconciliation.publication_rule: Do not combine the legacy directory list with planned construction features into an unsupported current amenity inventory.

address_reconciliation.finding: The current City event location and official Park Points GIS agree on 2165 Wilmington Highway. The event record supplies ZIP 28306. The City park parcel uses 2161 Wilmington Highway as its property situs address; the legacy intake source used Old Wilmington Highway and ZIP 28301.
address_reconciliation.publication_rule: Use 2165 Wilmington Highway, Fayetteville, NC 28306 as the current visitor address. Retain 2161 only as parcel context and the Old Wilmington/28301 form only as legacy evidence, not alternate public entrances.

current_access_review.finding: Current City shelter-rental records, the December 2025 public event record, and the January 2026 County trail-extension action establish active public use. No current Arnette Park page or operator source with general daily hours was found.
current_access_review.publication_rule: Do not reuse the 2013 seasonal schedule as current hours. Recheck the operator or obtain written confirmation before launch-guide publication.

identity_reconciliation.finding: The current City park page and A-Z directory place Spring Forest Road Park at 4203 Spring Forest Road. The same directory separately places Millbrook Exchange Park at 1905 Spring Forest Road. The submitted 4203 address is therefore not a duplicate of Millbrook Exchange Park.
identity_reconciliation.publication_rule: Retain Spring Forest Road Park as a distinct parent. Do not substitute Millbrook Exchange Park or its 1905 Spring Forest Road address.

current_access_review.finding: The park page was updated July 15, 2026 and lists current facilities and rental guidance. The linked Citywide park rules state dawn-to-dusk hours unless otherwise posted; the park page separately states that court lighting operates from dusk to 10 p.m.
current_access_review.publication_rule: Use dawn to dusk as the general park rule with the explicit unless-otherwise-posted qualification. Treat the court-lighting statement as facility-specific guidance, not a blanket extension of every park use.
